title: Exclusion from Temporary Import Rules
summary: This thread tracks the exclusion of privileged persons from temporary import regulations for machinery and equipment. The scope remains consistent, but the legal instrument evolves to reflect updated 2025 regulations.

evolution.scope: Maintains consistent exclusion criteria while updating the governing instrument.

timeline.change: Establishment of exclusion for privileged persons from temporary import rules.
Re-codification of the exclusion under the 2025 framework.

১। শিরোনাম, প্রয়োজনীয়তা ও প্রবর্তন।—(১) এই বিধিমালা পণ্য-যন্ত্রপাতি, যন্ত্রাংশ ও সরঞ্জাম ফেরতের ভিত্তিতে সাময়িক আমদানি বিধিমালা, ২০২২ নামে অভিহিত হইবে।
(২) এই বিধিমালা নিম্নবর্ণিত ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য হইবে না, যথা:—
(ক) কূটনৈতিক এবং Privileged Persons (Customs Procedure) Rules, 2003 এর rule 2 এর clause (d) এ সংজ্ঞায়িত Privileged Persons কর্তৃক আমদানিকৃত কোনো পণ্য-যন্ত্রপাতি, যন্ত্রাংশ ও সরঞ্জাম;
(খ) Customs Act, 1969 এর FIRST SCHEDULE এ বর্ণিত Heading 87.02 এর HS Code ও Heading 87.03 এর HS Code এর অন্তর্গত পণ্য-যন্ত্রপাতি, যন্ত্রাংশ ও সরঞ্জাম আমদানি; এবং
(গ) কোনো প্রকল্পে বা প্ল্যান্টে বা মেশিনে বা সুনির্দিষ্ট কোনো উদ্দেশ্যে ব্যবহারের লক্ষ্যে আমদানিকৃত ভোগ্যপণ্য (consumable products) যাহা উক্ত প্রকল্পে বা প্ল্যান্টে বা মেশিনে বা উক্ত উদ্দেশ্যে ব্যবহারের ফলে আংশিক বা সম্পূর্ণভাবে নিঃশেষিত হয় বা ব্যবহারের অনুপযোগী হয়।
(৩) এই বিধিমালা অবিলম্বে কার্যকর হইবে।

Temporary Import of Goods, Machinery, Pa: This set of rules is officially titled the Temporary Import of Goods, Machinery, Parts and Equipment Rules 2022 and comes into effect immediately.
Privileged Persons (Customs Procedures): These rules exclude goods, machinery, parts, and equipment imported by privileged persons as defined under the specific clauses of these existing rules from the scope of the new regulations.
H.S. Code: Goods, machinery, parts, and equipment falling under specific headings of the Customs tariff are exempt from the application of these rules.
Consumable Goods: Consumable goods intended for use in projects, plants, or machinery that are partially or fully depleted or rendered unusable through their application are explicitly excluded from these rules.
Customs Act 1969: The First Schedule of the Customs Act 1969 provides the tariff structure and headings used to define the scope of exclusions within these rules.
First Schedule: The First Schedule of the Customs Act 1969 is referenced to determine specific classifications of goods excluded from the provisions of this rule.

Temporary Import of Goods, Machinery, Pa: These rules establish the regulatory framework for the temporary importation of goods, machinery, parts, and equipment based on return conditions. The rules come into effect on June 2, 2025.
Privileged Persons (Customs Procedures): These rules provide specific exemptions, excluding goods imported by privileged persons defined under their provisions from the scope of the Temporary Import of Goods, Machinery, Parts and Equipment Rules 2025.
Consumable Goods: Consumable goods listed in the schedule of the rules, which are intended for use in projects, plants, or machinery and are partially or fully consumed or rendered unusable during such use, are excluded from the scope of these rules.

Specific categories of consumable goods subject to these provisions include steel sheets, steel rods, steel pipes, cement, boulder stones, tiles, prefabricated buildings, piles and poles, lighting fittings, transmission towers, specific types of cables, distribution transformers, paints and varnishes, household goods, chemicals, lubricating and transformer oils, office equipment, air conditioners up to a certain capacity, dredgers, anchor boats, and various motor vehicles.
Steel Sheet: Specified as a consumable good, this includes steel sheets of six millimeters or less meeting specific international testing standards.
Paint: Categorized as a consumable good for the purposes of these rules.
Household Goods: Listed as a category of consumable goods excluded from the temporary import facility.
Chemicals: Included in the schedule of consumable goods that do not qualify for the temporary import procedure.
Air Conditioner: Air conditioners with a cooling capacity not exceeding a specified threshold are classified as consumable goods and are excluded from the scope of these rules.
Anchor Boat: Anchor boats are identified as consumable goods and are therefore excluded from the provisions of these rules.
Customs Act 2023: The first schedule of this Act is referenced to define specific categories of motor vehicles that are excluded from the temporary import rules as consumable goods.
